rounds.title: My AI agent deleted the roadmap
rounds.context: A founder-style professional-network post. Judge the writing.
rounds.body:
This morning, I asked our AI agent to prioritize the roadmap.

It deleted the backlog.

At first, I called it a bug. Then I realized: our customers had never asked for a backlog. They asked for outcomes.

We now have zero technical debt, zero missed deadlines, and zero features.

The board calls it a shutdown. I call it radical focus.

What has your AI agent taught you about leadership? #BuildInPublic #AgenticEverything
rounds.explanation: AI wrote this original satire for the game. The inspirational pivot turns a disastrous product decision into a leadership lesson. It is a fictional post, not a quotation or screenshot from a real founder.
rounds.discussion: Which line made you laugh? Would you have believed it on a professional feed?
rounds.source: Original AI-written fictional professional-network post, October 4, 2026. No real person or company is depicted.

rounds.title: The football upgrade nobody asked for
rounds.context: Inspect the players and their equipment. Judge the image origin.
rounds.alt: A historical black-and-white photograph of people playing football while riding motorcycles.
rounds.explanation: Motorcycle football was real. This photograph is preserved by the German Federal Archives and dated August 1931. Strange inventions existed long before image generators.
rounds.discussion: Did the absurd premise make you overlook the ordinary photographic details?
rounds.source: Bundesarchiv, Bild 102-12210 / CC-BY-SA 3.0 Germany. Photographer unrecorded; August 1931. Commons version cropped in 2024; app copy re-encoded as JPEG without generative edits. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/de/deed.en

rounds.title: The voice behind the demo
rounds.context: A short English voice sample. Judge how the voice was produced, not who wrote its words.
rounds.body: Press Play, listen once or twice, then choose AI or HUMAN.
rounds.explanation: This is the official Alloy voice example embedded in OpenAI's text-to-speech guide. The speech is synthesized. A natural delivery and ordinary wording do not establish a human speaker.
rounds.discussion: Did you judge the voice, the script, or the recording quality?
rounds.source: OpenAI, official Alloy synthetic-voice example in the text-to-speech guide. Linked from its original host; not redistributed in the archive. Retrieved October 4, 2026.

rounds.title: Perfectly normal office lighting
rounds.context: A person reads beside an electrical experiment. Judge whether AI created this image.
rounds.alt: A seated person reading near large electrical equipment and bright arcs in a historical photograph.
rounds.explanation: The famous Tesla laboratory publicity photograph dates to December 1899. It is a human-made double exposure: the electrical arcs and Tesla were photographed separately. HUMAN does not mean the scene happened exactly as pictured.
rounds.discussion: Would you have called it fake? Is fake the same thing as AI-generated?
rounds.source: Dickenson V. Alley, Tesla laboratory photograph, December 1899; Commons public-domain-US record. Historical double exposure, resized/re-encoded for this app; no generative edits.

rounds.title: A network with feathers
rounds.context: Two short excerpts from a networking document. Judge the original writing.
rounds.body:
The scroll of paper is wrapped around one leg of the avian carrier.

[...]

The bandwidth is limited to the leg length.
rounds.explanation: David Waitzman wrote RFC 1149 in 1990: a deliberately silly April Fools networking specification for carrying IP datagrams by birds. Engineers were writing deadpan nonsense long before ChatGPT.
rounds.discussion: Did the formal vocabulary make this feel more or less generated?
rounds.source: David Waitzman, RFC 1149, April 1, 1990. Two exact sentences from Frame Format, separated by a marked omission. 21 quoted words; no translation.

rounds.title: An unexpected guest at the coronation
rounds.context: Inspect the guests in this imperial painting. Then choose AI or HUMAN.
rounds.alt: An imperial ceremony painting with ornate robes and a grey-coated guest among the crowd.
rounds.explanation: This is an original AI-generated historical pastiche. Inspector Gadget has slipped into the crowd, complete with a mechanical arm. It is not an authentic Napoleon painting, and no museum record is claimed.
rounds.discussion: Who spotted the guest first? Could a human artist have painted the same joke?
rounds.source: OpenAI built-in image generation, October 4, 2026. Original fictional imperial ceremony; Inspector Gadget cameo. Resized/re-encoded; full prompt in ContentSources.md.

rounds.title: The family IT department
rounds.context: An English excerpt from a computing lecture. Judge the voice's origin.
rounds.body: Listen to the recording, then vote. Speaker and date appear after the reveal.
rounds.alt: A short English excerpt from a computing lecture.
rounds.explanation: This is Grace Hopper's actual voice from her 1982 lecture to the NSA. She jokes about a parent needing to ask his three children for computer time. The excerpt is trimmed and encoded to MP3; the voice is not cloned.
rounds.discussion: Did the old recording make you trust it? Could a synthetic voice imitate those recording flaws?
rounds.source: Grace Hopper / NSA, Future Possibilities: Data, Hardware, Software, and People, August 19, 1982. Public-domain US government recording released in 2024. Short original-voice excerpt; exact interval in ContentSources.md.

rounds.title: The new hire seems qualified
rounds.context: A mainframe team photo. Look beyond the serious faces.
rounds.alt: A black-and-white mainframe room with formally dressed workers and a cat at the central terminal.
rounds.explanation: AI generated this fictional archival team photograph, including the cat in a tie operating the terminal. Film grain, dated equipment and a deadpan cast were requested deliberately.
rounds.discussion: Is the cat proof of AI, or merely proof that somebody wanted a joke?
rounds.source: OpenAI built-in image generation, October 4, 2026. Original fictional 1960s computer-room photograph. Resized/re-encoded; full prompt in ContentSources.md.

rounds.title: The robots have better moves than us
rounds.context: Judge the footage: camera recording or generated video? A robot in a camera recording can still be HUMAN content.
rounds.body: Play the short clip. Sound is optional for this round.
rounds.alt: A short clip of robots dancing in a robotics laboratory.
rounds.explanation: Boston Dynamics filmed its real robots performing a choreographed dance. HUMAN here describes the human-produced camera footage, not a claim that the robots contain no software or autonomy.
rounds.discussion: Did convincing movement make you think of CGI or generative video?
rounds.source: Boston Dynamics, Do You Love Me?, official YouTube upload, December 29, 2020. Embedded excerpt 00:00–00:18; original footage and soundtrack remain on YouTube.

rounds.title: The astronaut took the scenic route
rounds.context: A short space-themed street scene. Judge the footage, not whether the story sounds sensible.
rounds.body: Press Play and inspect movement, the suit and the street.
rounds.alt: An astronaut running through a colorful urban alley.
rounds.explanation: Runway publishes this clip as a Gen-3 Alpha output: an astronaut running through an alley in Rio de Janeiro. The official source states that the videos on that page were generated with the model.
rounds.discussion: Would this have fooled you if it appeared in a behind-the-scenes film clip?
rounds.source: Runway, Introducing Gen-3 Alpha, June 17, 2024; astronaut-in-Rio demo, carousel-01 output-002. Linked from the original host, not redistributed; official demo watermark retained.
